solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great enthusiasm — not so many half-hearted, by the look of it

indicators.text: half-hearted, by the look of it
indicators.note: the heart of the word for 'not so many' is a W, and a V looks like half a W, so the middle letter is swapped for its visual half

parts.note: fewer means not so many

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a crowd's great enthusiasm is waning, with fewer and fewer half-hearted supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is visual: V is drawn as one half of W, so 'half-hearted' cuts the central W of FEWER down to a V.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever of excitement is a state of intense, eager enthusiasm, a common figurative sense.

clue.text: Colour of cosmetic that's at the bottom of the pile?

definitions.text: that's at the bottom of the pile?

parts.note: foundation is a make-up base applied to the face
stone is a pale greyish-beige shade name

explanation.surface: A make-up question about the shade of a foundation product, oddly tied to a heap of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' means a building here, not a heap of washing or hair; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial first block laid at the base of a building literally sits beneath the whole edifice.

clue.text: Personage meeting queen's a treacherous type

parts.note: a personage is a very important person, a VIP
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A dignitary meets the monarch, and someone at court proves to be a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake in the grass: a venomous serpent is the standard figure for a treacherous person.

clue.text: Agent needs to mingle to succeed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
to lace is to intertwine or mix in, as lacing coffee with brandy

explanation.surface: Advice that a spy or salesperson must mix with people to get on in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' looks like 'do well' but means 'come after' here.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to take their place after them, as an heir follows a monarch.

clue.text: Rebel section taking a copper on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside it, so these pieces go within the ship's letters

parts.note: board here points to a ship, a steamship being SS

indicators.note: the section takes the following pieces, so they are joined on after it

parts.note: a part is a section
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A rebellious faction of the mob has a policeman hostage on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword stock phrase for placing letters inside SS, the steamship abbreviation; 'copper' is the metal, not the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator led the great slave revolt against Rome, the archetypal insurgent.

clue.text: Second class advocate

parts.note: ilk means kind or class

explanation.surface: A sneer at a mediocre lawyer: a second-rate barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a Queen's or King's Counsel is called a silk, from the silk gown senior barristers wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior British barrister, entitled to the silk gown, is informally known by the fabric.

clue.text: A male running through inclined section of theatre

indicators.note: one piece runs through the middle of another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: prone means inclined, as in prone to errors
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A man dashes across a sloping part of a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined section' tempts as a raked stage, but 'inclined' supplies PRONE, which STAG runs through.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a stage projecting in front of the curtain toward the audience bears this name.

clue.text: Presenting bill before the fish

indicators.note: the bill comes ahead of the fish in the answer

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A diner is shown the bill before the fish course arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion, the opposite of the American sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a proposal forward formally for debate is tabling it in British usage.

clue.text: Join forces and manage to involve old class

indicators.note: the word for manage takes in a letter, so it wraps around it

parts.note: to cope is to manage
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Teammates combine efforts and handle a former classmate group.
explanation.definitionFit: To collaborate or work together toward a common aim is to unite efforts.

clue.text: New location of permanent stairs not entirely clear

indicators.note: the letters are moved to new positions, an arrangement signal

explanation.surface: A property note about moving a fixed staircase, and the result being murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something partly see-through lets light pass but is not fully clear, like frosted glass.

clue.text: Disliked local inhabitants leaving church in unseemly run

indicators.note: the trimmed inhabitants go inside the rearranged run
unseemly means improper or disorderly, so the letters of run are disordered
the church's letters depart from the word for inhabitants

parts.note: the populace are the people of a place
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A politician hated by locals, the faithful walking out amid a disgraceful campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a campaign or sprint, but it is only three letters to rearrange, and 'unseemly' is their signal; the trimmed inhabitants then go inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disliked by people is being out of favour, the plain sense.

clue.text: What's used for clearing shrub

definitions.meaning: a brush with a long handle used for sweeping floors
a yellow-flowered leguminous bush common on heathland

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool for tidying up undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a sweeping brush and the bushy plant once used to make one.

clue.text: Wayward lads holding men back

indicators.note: the rearranged lads hold the next piece within them
wayward means unruly or straying, so the letters of lads go astray

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is crossword shorthand for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Unruly youths restrain some men from going forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is an adjective-like definition: 'Wayward' makes DSAL from LADS, holding OR. 'Back' looks like part of 'holding men back' but stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical adjective describes the back, as a dolphin's fin on its upper side.

clue.text: Crooked servicemen taken in charge

indicators.note: the servicemen are taken into the word for charge

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army servicemen

explanation.surface: Bent soldiers are arrested and charged.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout path is not straight, so crooked and devious in route.

clue.text: Self-evident blunders — all but leader for the high jump?

indicators.note: the letters blunder about into a new arrangement
everything except the first letter is kept, so the leading letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Obvious mistakes have made someone liable for severe punishment, except the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the high jump' sounds like 'in trouble', but it means a category the high jump belongs to. 'all but leader' drops the S, leaving ELFEVIDENT to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics contests off the track, such as the high jump or discus, form this category.

clue.text: Sum that man arrived at slashed by 50, without reservation

parts.note: a tot is a sum, as in to tot up
he means that man

indicators.note: the word for arrived at is cut through by the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: to hit a target or figure is to arrive at it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An accountant's fit of total calculation cut by fifty, offered with full commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to the handle of a sword plunged in fully: an idiom for completely, entirely.

clue.text: Row about heroin and crack's comparatively sparing

indicators.note: the row goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
H is slang for heroin
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: A drug-themed argument over heroin and crack, ending in thrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a line of seats, not a quarrel; 'crack' is a split, not the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more economical or frugal with money than another is the comparative of careful saving.

clue.text: A verse in summer month about fruit

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Aug is short for August

explanation.surface: A poem written in August about a tropical fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree yields this pear-shaped edible produce with pink or white flesh.

clue.text: Victorian craftsman releasing mass preparation for perfumier

indicators.note: the craftsman lets go of a letter, which is removed

parts.note: William Morris was a leading Victorian designer and craftsman of the Arts and Crafts movement

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century artisan frees his workforce, perhaps, while making scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered iris root, violet-scented, is a fixative used in making perfumes.

clue.text: You reflected bilingually, interrupting the lady's sleep

indicators.note: the reflected word breaks into the lady, sitting inside her

parts.note: she is the lady; the 's is read as 'is'

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: the second language gives the French word for you, tu
ye is the old English you

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of you in two languages while disturbing a woman's nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' works twice over, as the clue's 'bilingually' signals: TU in French, reversed by 'reflected' to UT, and YE in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial term for a nap or rest, from closing the eyes.

clue.text: There's frivolity when Verity takes the other side

indicators.note: right is swapped for its opposite side, left, so R gives way to L

parts.note: verity is truth or correctness, rightness

explanation.surface: A woman called Verity switches sides, and things get silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verity' looks like a name but means truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of seriousness, a light-hearted manner, is a synonym for flippancy.

clue.text: Forces taking a turn, discussions announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: talks are discussions

explanation.surface: Negotiations take a new direction, as officially declared.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics these are rotational forces, the twisting effect that makes a body turn.

clue.text: Tons of jam taken out, applied and thoroughly spread

indicators.note: the letter for tons is removed from the word for jam

parts.note: to jam is to cram or stuff
used means applied, as applied a tool

explanation.surface: A pot of jam is opened and spread generously on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permeated or overspread, like a sky flushed with colour, is diffused throughout.

clue.text: A queen borne by supporter's one revered in India

indicators.note: the queen and the A are carried after the supporter in the answer

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment; the 's is read as 'is'
HM, Her Majesty, is a queen

explanation.surface: A monarch is carried along by a loyal follower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu creator god, one of the great trinity, is a deity worshipped in the subcontinent.

clue.text: Hurl back what Adolf's mate brought up

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?

indicators.note: in a down light, bringing a word up reverses it

parts.note: Eva Braun was Adolf Hitler's companion

explanation.surface: Throwing back what Hitler's companion vomited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests being sick, hinting at the other sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something heavy with effort, a synonym for fling or toss.

clue.text: Cautious European ducks all in

indicators.note: to duck out is to dodge or leave, so the letter drops out

parts.note: all in means exhausted, tired out

explanation.surface: A European is wiped out among the waterfowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarded and on the alert for danger, a synonym for careful or circumspect.

clue.text: Cow's lacking breadth of sheep

indicators.note: the cattle adjective goes without one letter

parts.note: bovine means of or like cattle

explanation.surface: A cow lacks the bulk of a sheep, a farmyard comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing sheep and their kind, from the Latin for ewe.

clue.text: Throw out flag almost adopted by Brussels — not before time!

indicators.note: the trimmed flag is taken in by the Brussels letters, sitting inside

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union

indicators.note: almost the whole flag is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: a jack is a flag flown by a ship
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: The EU belatedly takes up a new flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' is an old sense of the answer, to cry out or eject suddenly; 'Brussels' stands for the European Union headquartered there.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim suddenly or eject forcibly, a dated sense of uttering or expelling.

clue.text: Being one of the first presumably to admit retreat, sincerely

indicators.note: the word for being first lets in the next piece, which goes inside

parts.words: Being one of the first presumably
parts.note: early arrivals are among the first to come
a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A pioneer, presumably among the first, earnestly owns up to backing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with serious, heartfelt conviction is the same as doing so genuinely.

clue.text: Delightful playing partners arranged to go round

indicators.note: the arranged word encircles the partners

parts.note: set means arranged, as a table is set
in bridge West and East are partners, W and E

explanation.surface: Bridge partners are seated so as to circulate, a pleasant arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and lovely, a common sense of the word beyond sugary taste.
